title: Standard pair of subcategories on the constructible categories
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, the field $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and a scheme $Y$.

1. *Integral level.* For a finite extension $E/\Ql$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi_E$, let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and for an object $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$ let $\mathcal H^r(K)$ be its $r$-th cohomology sheaf in the abelian category $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put
$$
 D^{\le0}_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)=\{K:\mathcal H^r(K)=0\ \text{for all } r>0\},\qquad
 D^{\ge0}_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)=\{K:\mathcal H^r(K)=0\ \text{for all } r<0\}.
$$

2. *Rational level.* The rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] has the same objects as $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Let $D^{\le0}_c(Y,E)$ (resp. $D^{\ge0}_c(Y,E)$) be the class of objects $K$ of $D^b_c(Y,E)$ that are isomorphic in $D^b_c(Y,E)$ to some $L\in D^{\le0}_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ (resp. $L\in D^{\ge0}_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$).

3. *Algebraically closed level.* Let $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)=\mathcal C_Y$ be the common-stage category of pairs $(E,K)$, $E$ in the directed set $\mathcal E_\ell$ of finite extensions of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $D^{\le0}_c(Y,\Qlb)$ (resp. $D^{\ge0}_c(Y,\Qlb)$) be the class of objects $X$ of $\mathcal C_Y$ that are isomorphic in $\mathcal C_Y$ to some $(L,M)$ with $L\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $M\in D^{\le0}_c(Y,L)$ (resp. $M\in D^{\ge0}_c(Y,L)$).

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ use the cohomological shift $[n]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and put $D^{\le n}_c(Y,\Lambda)=\{K:K[n]\in D^{\le0}_c(Y,\Lambda)\}$ and $D^{\ge n}_c(Y,\Lambda)=\{K:K[n]\in D^{\ge0}_c(Y,\Lambda)\}$. The pair $(D^{\le0}_c(Y,\Lambda),D^{\ge0}_c(Y,\Lambda))$ is the *standard pair* on $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$; all its classes are closed under isomorphism by construction. That it is a bounded $t$-structure [def-weil-t-structure] (for $Y$ of finite type over $k$) is a separate statement, not part of this definition.

lean.note: §1(B): the earlier ConstructibleStandardTStructure declarations use the legacy bounded integral and rational categories, whereas the recorded integral, rational, common-stage and derived-pullback interfaces now use the intrinsic sf categories.
